This application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking following relief:-
"It is therefore, prayed in the interest of Justice, this application / petition may kindly

Crime No.28/19 at Badgonda, Indore Distt. Indore."

sentences.text: The Fir No.28/19 in Police Station Bodgonda, District Indore
has been registered against the applicant for offence under Section 376 of IPC.
3. I.A. No.30296/2021 has been filed for quashment of proceedings on the basis of compromise.
4. Considered the submissions made by counsel for the parties.

5. The Supreme Court in the case of Narinder Singh and Others Vs. State of Punjab and Others reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466 has held as under:-

sentences.text: Such a power is not to be exercised in those prosecutions which involve heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc.
Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society.

Similarly, for the offences alleged to have been committed under special statute like the Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity are not to be quashed merely on the basis of compromise between the victim and the offender."
6.

Thus it is clear that the power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is not to be exercised in the prosecutions which involve heinous and serious offences of mental depravity like murder, rape,
dacoity, etc.
Therefore, the application for quashment of FIR on the basis of compromise is hereby rejected.
7. It is further submitted by counsel for the applicant that if the FIR is read in its entirety, the prosecutrix herself was a consenting party.
Furthermore, according to the FIR, the applicant had married the prosecutrix on 09/12/2011 in a Temple situated in hotel Uphaar in Mhow and thereafter he had physical relations with her.
On the pretext that he would get the marriage registered, he was continuously sexually exploiting her.
In the month of November, 2018, again he came to Raipur and raped her.
Later on, she got an information from reliable sources that the applicant has already performed engagement ceremony and wants to go to abroad and he has already left two women.

8. Challenging the FIR lodged by the prosecutrix, it is submitted by counsel for the applicant that since the applicant had performed marriage on 09/12/2011, therefore, it cannot be said that the applicant had raped her.
However, fairly conceded that both the parties were NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26701 married and their first marriage was subsisting.

Furthermore,
according to the FIR, the applicant married the prosecutrix in a Temple situated in hotel Uphaar,
Mhow.
Since the applicant himself was a married person, therefore, he was aware of the fact that his second marriage during the subsistence of first marriage is not possible.
Therefore, it is clear that in fact the applicant has voluntarily made the prosecutrix to believe that she is the legally wedded wife of the applicant.

Furthermore, consent of the prosecurix was obtained by misconception of fact and,
therefore, in the light of Section 90 of IPC, her consent cannot be said to be a free consent.
From the connected case M.Cr.C. No.46581/2019, it is clear that the applicant was granted anticipatory bail on the ground that he will get the marriage registered, but even that was not done.
Furthermore, IA No.8490/2022 was filed by previous counsel alleging that by flouting the orders passed by the Court, applicant has shifted to Canada.
Thus, it is clear that even otherwise the applicant has left the country without permission of the Court.

9. Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that no case is made out for quashment of FIR in Crime No.28/2019 registered at Police Station Badgonda, District Indore for offence under Section 376 of IPC.
10.
Accordingly, the application fails and is hereby dismissed.
